div.p: Purchase confidence
Two friends, one practical idea — tech that builds community, not landfill.

From childhood friends to Dads navigating rising costs and a world that feels stretched, Louis and Drew built the Re-Ware Project for one reason — everyone deserves access to technology, without compromising the planet our kids will inherit.
Louis and Drew grew up together and have always shared the same values — helping people and protecting the environment.

Louis runs Co-Creative IT, a generational family business that's worked across the tech space for years. That insight showed him how devices are used throughout their lifespan. When he started seeing perfectly viable tech heading to landfill, the path forward was clear.

Together, they created a system that makes refurbished devices accessible and affordable. Which led them to develop the Re-Ware Project — a straightforward way to give reliable devices a second life and donate them to people who actually need them rather than sending them to landfill.
Re-Ware partners with corporates, not-for-profits and community minded organisations to build practical circular solutions that keep devices in use, not waste streams.
We operate simply, building long-term partnerships, clear communication, and solutions designed around real needs.

It's not charity, and it's not corporate spin. It's just a better way to use what already exists and make technology part of community, not landfill. If that approach makes sense to you, we'd love to talk.
We believe that together, we can create a more sustainable and digitally inclusive future for all.

Re-Ware refurbishes suitable devices and donates them to Western Australians experiencing digital poverty — including lower-income individuals and families, people that are displaced, people with disabilities, justice programs, and to support women and children rebuilding after domestic violence who need safe digital access.

img.alt: Donate devices to help close the digital divide for women and children in Perth

div.h2: Digital poverty is growing — but it's preventable. By choosing Re-Ware, you're contributing to:

div.p: Re-Ware gives tech a second life and provides disadvantaged Western Australians with a first chance at learning. Refurbished devices go straight to schools, students, and community programs, helping those in need get online and reach their full educational potential.
We believe access to education should reflect the values of our broader community: looking after each other, regardless of circumstance — because education shouldn't be determined by privilege.

Access to tech, access to opportunity. In today's job market, digital skills and access to technology are essential. Without reliable devices, many people face barriers to finding work, participating in online training, and keeping up with the changing demands of the workplace.

By donating refurbished devices and supporting digital confidence, we give people the tools to explore opportunities, complete training, and connect with new career pathways — helping more Western Australians participate fully in the workforce.

Reliable tech isn't just convenient — it's essential. Without devices and internet access, many Western Australians face challenges managing everyday tasks like food shopping, banking, healthcare, vital services, accessing essential resources, and taking care of important responsibilities.

Re-Ware helps bridge that gap. Essential access shouldn't depend on circumstance, so we're working to make it possible for everyone to access what they need, when they need it, and participate fully in daily life.
Responsibly sustainable. Refurbishing just two desktop computers saves 797 kg of CO₂ — consider it a little boost to your good-karma bank.
That's the same as:

ul.li: Driving a heavy goods vehicle 937 km.
Hauling 50 tonnes of freight across 1,000 km.

div.p: E-waste reduction: Re-Ware Project can provide a full history of every device we work on and quantify your CO₂ savings annually through our sustainability calculator.

Devices that bring people together. Being able to communicate easily is essential for building relationships, sharing experiences, and feeling part of a community. Without access to technology, many people can feel isolated or cut off from the people and support networks that matter most.

With rising rates of mental health challenges and depression in Western Australia, limited access to technology can leave people feeling isolated. Re-Ware Project helps people engage with their communities, join social activities, and strengthen the bonds that make everyday life richer.

div.h2: Your clean-up done right = a meaningful local outcome.

div.p: We invite you to join us in making a tangible difference in our community through the Re-Ware Project. As a company dedicated to creativity, innovation, social and environmental responsibility, Co-Creative IT has designed Re-Ware Project to address digital poverty and environmental challenges head-on.
Interested in working together? Fill out some info and we will be in touch shortly. We can't wait to hear from you!
